title: Square-zero gluing for fibred groupoids
statement: Work over $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes, with its actual fibre categories and cartesian arrows [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Say that $\mathcal F$ satisfies square-zero gluing (RS*) if for every diagram of commutative rings $A\to B\leftarrow B'$ with $B'\to B$ surjective and square-zero kernel, restriction gives an equivalence $\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_B B'))\simeq\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)\times_{\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)}\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B')$. The right side is the groupoid of a pair of objects with a specified isomorphism of their restrictions and pairs of arrows compatible with that isomorphism. Equivalently, every span of cartesian arrows from an object over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ to the two given objects has a gluing over the ring pullback, universal on arrows in that fibre. Here the integer base, its canonical scheme structures, fibre objects and arrows over specified base maps are those of [def-sfb-artin-integer-base-versality].
